problems.title: Find Maximum Element in Array
problems.description: Given an array of integers, find and print the largest element.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n (number of elements). Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print the maximum element.
hints: Scan the array once, keeping the largest value seen so far.
Initialise the maximum with the first element, not with 0, so all-negative arrays work.

problems.title: Find Second-Largest Element
problems.description: Given an array of integers with at least two distinct values, find the second-largest distinct element.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print the second-largest distinct element.
problems.constraints: 2 <= n <= 10^5, -10^9 <= element <= 10^9, at least two distinct values exist
hints: Track the largest and second-largest values in a single pass.
Duplicates of the maximum must not count as the second largest.

problems.title: Reverse an Array
problems.description: Given an array, print its elements in reverse order.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers (omitted when n = 0).
problems.outputFormat: Print the elements in reverse order, space-separated. Print an empty line when n = 0.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        print('')
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    arr = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    print(' '.join(map(str, reversed(arr))))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: You can reverse with two pointers swapping from both ends.
Reversing in place uses O(1) extra space.

problems.title: Check Palindrome String
problems.description: Given a string of lowercase letters, determine whether it reads the same forwards and backwards.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing the string (lowercase letters only).
problems.outputFormat: Print 'true' if the string is a palindrome, otherwise 'false' (all lowercase).
hints: Compare characters from both ends moving toward the centre.
A single character (and the empty string) is a palindrome.

problems.title: Reverse Vowels of a String
problems.description: Reverse only the vowels of a string, keeping all other characters in their original positions. Vowels are a, e, i, o, u (both cases).
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing the string (letters only).
problems.outputFormat: Print the string with its vowels reversed.
hints: Use two pointers: one from the start, one from the end, skipping non-vowels.
Swap only when both pointers are on vowels.

problems.title: Check Anagrams
problems.description: Given two strings of lowercase letters, determine whether one is an anagram of the other (same letters, same counts, possibly different order).
problems.inputFormat: Two lines: the first string, then the second string.
problems.outputFormat: Print 'true' if the strings are anagrams, otherwise 'false' (all lowercase).

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    a = lines[0] if len(lines) > 0 else ''
    b = lines[1] if len(lines) > 1 else ''
    from collections import Counter
    print('true' if Counter(a) == Counter(b) else 'false')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Anagrams have identical character counts - compare frequency maps.
Different lengths can never be anagrams; check that first.

problems.title: Factorial of a Number
problems.description: Given a non-negative integer n, compute n! (the product of all positive integers up to n). By definition, 0! = 1.
problems.inputFormat: A single integer n.
problems.outputFormat: Print n! as an integer.
hints: Multiply 1 x 2 x ... x n in a loop.
Remember 0! = 1. In JavaScript, use BigInt for n > 20.

problems.title: Check Prime Number
problems.description: Given an integer n, determine whether it is a prime number (divisible only by 1 and itself, and greater than 1).
problems.inputFormat: A single integer n.
problems.outputFormat: Print 'true' if n is prime, otherwise 'false' (all lowercase).
hints: Only test divisors up to sqrt(n): if n has a factor larger than sqrt(n), the co-factor is smaller.
0 and 1 are not prime. 2 is the only even prime.

problems.title: Trailing Zeros in Factorial
problems.description: Given n, count how many trailing zeros n! has in decimal representation, without computing n! itself.
problems.inputFormat: A single integer n.
problems.outputFormat: Print the number of trailing zeros in n!.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
    count = 0
    p = 5
    while p <= n:
        count += n // p
        p *= 5
    print(count)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Each trailing zero comes from a factor 10 = 2 x 5; factors of 5 are scarcer, so count them.
Count floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + ...

problems.title: Sum of Digits
problems.description: Given a non-negative integer, compute the sum of its decimal digits.
problems.inputFormat: A single non-negative integer.
problems.outputFormat: Print the sum of its digits.
problems.timeComplexity: O(d) where d is the number of digits
hints: Repeatedly take n % 10 (last digit) and then n = n // 10.
Handle 0 separately: the loop never runs, so the answer stays 0.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Given an array and a target value, find two distinct indices i, j (i < j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] = target. Exactly one solution exists.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: integer target.
problems.outputFormat: Print the two indices i and j, space-separated, with i < j.
problems.constraints: 2 <= n <= 10^5, -10^9 <= element, target <= 10^9, exactly one solution
hints: For each element x, check whether target - x was seen before.
Store each value's index in a hash map as you scan left to right.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.description: Given a sorted array, remove the duplicates in place (conceptually) and print the array with each distinct value appearing once, in order.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
problems.outputFormat: Print the deduplicated array, space-separated. Print an empty line when n = 0.
hints: Because the input is sorted, duplicates are adjacent.
Keep a write pointer: copy an element only when it differs from the previous kept one.

problems.title: Pair with Given Sum
problems.description: Given an array and a target value, determine whether any two distinct elements sum to the target.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: integer target.
problems.outputFormat: Print 'YES' if such a pair exists, otherwise 'NO'.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    arr = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    target = int(data[1 + n])
    seen = set()
    for x in arr:
        if target - x in seen:
            print('YES')
            return
        seen.add(x)
    print('NO')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: This is the existence version of Two Sum: a hash set is enough.
If the array were sorted, two pointers from both ends would use O(1) space.

problems.title: Maximum Average Subarray of Size K
problems.description: Given an array and an integer k, find the maximum average of any contiguous subarray of length exactly k.
problems.inputFormat: First line: two integers n and k. Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print the maximum average rounded to 2 decimal places.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    arr = list(map(int, data[2:2 + n]))
    window = sum(arr[:k])
    best = window
    for i in range(k, n):
        window += arr[i] - arr[i - k]
        best = max(best, window)
    print(f'{best / k:.2f}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Slide a window of size k: add the new element, subtract the one that leaves.
Track the maximum window SUM, then divide by k once at the end.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters.
problems.inputFormat: A single line containing the string (letters and digits; may be empty).
problems.outputFormat: Print the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
hints: Sliding window: expand right, and when a repeat appears, jump the left edge past its previous occurrence.
Keep a map of each character's last index.

problems.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
problems.description: Given strings s and p (lowercase letters), find all starting indices of anagrams of p in s.
problems.inputFormat: Two lines: string s, then string p.
problems.outputFormat: Print the starting indices space-separated. Print -1 if there are none.
problems.constraints: 1 <= len(p) <= len(s) <= 10^5, or len(p) > len(s) is allowed (answer -1)

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    from collections import Counter
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    s = lines[0] if len(lines) > 0 else ''
    p = lines[1] if len(lines) > 1 else ''
    if len(p) > len(s) or not p:
        print(-1)
        return
    need = Counter(p)
    window = Counter(s[:len(p)])
    out = []
    if window == need:
        out.append(0)
    for i in range(len(p), len(s)):
        out_ch, in_ch = s[i - len(p)], s[i]
        window[out_ch] -= 1
        if window[out_ch] == 0:
            del window[out_ch]
        window[in_ch] += 1
        if window == need:
            out.append(i - len(p) + 1)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)) if out else -1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Slide a window of length len(p) over s and compare character counts.
Update counts incrementally when the window moves instead of recounting.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.description: Given an unsorted array, find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers present in it. The sequence need not be contiguous in the array.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print the length of the longest consecutive sequence.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        print(0)
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = set(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    best = 0
    for x in nums:
        if x - 1 not in nums:            # only start counting at sequence starts
            length, cur = 1, x
            while cur + 1 in nums:
                cur += 1
                length += 1
            best = max(best, length)
    print(best)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Put the numbers in a set for O(1) lookups.
Only start counting from numbers whose predecessor is missing - that keeps the total work O(n).

problems.title: Contains Duplicate II (Nearby Duplicates)
problems.description: Given an array and an integer k, determine whether there are two distinct indices i, j with nums[i] == nums[j] and |i - j| <= k.
problems.inputFormat: First line: two integers n and k. Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print 'true' if such a pair exists, otherwise 'false' (all lowercase).
hints: Remember the most recent index of each value.
A duplicate counts only when the distance to its previous occurrence is at most k.

problems.title: Count Subarrays with Sum K
problems.description: Given an array and an integer k, count the number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to k.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: integer k.
problems.outputFormat: Print the count of subarrays summing to k.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    from collections import defaultdict
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    arr = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    prefix_counts = defaultdict(int)
    prefix_counts[0] = 1
    prefix = count = 0
    for x in arr:
        prefix += x
        count += prefix_counts[prefix - k]
        prefix_counts[prefix] += 1
    print(count)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: A subarray (l..r) sums to k exactly when prefix[r] - prefix[l-1] = k.
Count how many previous prefix sums equal prefix - k as you scan.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses

problems.title: Min Stack

problems.inputFormat: First line: integer q (number of operations). Next q lines, one operation each: 'push x', 'pop', 'top' or 'getMin'. pop is only called on a non-empty stack.
problems.outputFormat: For each 'top' and 'getMin' operation, print its result on its own line.

push 0
push -3
getMin
pop
top
getMin

tests.input:

push 3
push 1
push 2
getMin
pop
getMin

8
push 5
push 4
push 4
getMin
pop
getMin
pop
getMin

hints: Keep a parallel stack of running minimums, one entry per pushed element.
On pop, discard the top of both stacks.

problems.title: Next Greater Element
problems.description: For each element of an array, find the first element to its right that is strictly greater. If none exists, use -1.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Print the next greater element for each position, space-separated.
hints: Scan from right to left with a monotonic decreasing stack.
Pop elements that are smaller or equal - they can never be anyone's next greater.

problems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
problems.description: Implement a FIFO queue using two stacks. Process a sequence of operations and print the result of each pop/peek/empty operation.
problems.inputFormat: First line: integer q. Next q lines, one operation each: 'push x', 'pop', 'peek' or 'empty'. pop/peek are only called on a non-empty queue.
problems.outputFormat: For 'pop' print the removed value, for 'peek' print the front value, for 'empty' print 'true' or 'false' - each on its own line.

examples.input:
6
push 1
push 2
peek
pop
peek
empty

tests.input:
6
push 1
push 2
push 3
pop
pop
peek

hints: Push onto stack A; pop/peek from stack B, refilling B from A (reversed) only when B is empty.
Refilling reverses the order, which is exactly what turns LIFO into FIFO.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.description: Given a linked list as a space-separated sequence of values, print the values in reverse order. (Input format: values in list order; the list is empty when the input is empty.)
problems.inputFormat: One line of space-separated integers, in list order. The line may be empty for an empty list.
problems.outputFormat: Print the values in reverse order, space-separated. Print an empty line for an empty list.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
    vals = list(map(int, line.split())) if line else []
    print(' '.join(map(str, reversed(vals))))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Iteratively rewire: prev = None; for each node, save next, point node.next to prev, advance.
With a real linked list this is O(1) extra space.

problems.title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
problems.description: A linked list is given as space-separated values, plus an integer pos: the 0-based index of the node the tail connects back to, or -1 if the tail connects to nothing. Determine whether the list has a cycle.
problems.inputFormat: First line: space-separated integers (the list values). Second line: integer pos (-1 means no cycle).
problems.outputFormat: Print 'true' if the list has a cycle, otherwise 'false' (all lowercase).

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    vals = list(map(int, lines[0].split())) if lines and lines[0].strip() else []
    pos = int(lines[1]) if len(lines) > 1 else -1
    print('true' if vals and pos != -1 else 'false')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: With real nodes, use Floyd's tortoise and hare: if fast meets slow, there is a cycle.
Here pos != -1 directly means the tail links back, which is exactly a cycle.

problems.title: Middle of Linked List
problems.description: Given a non-empty linked list as space-separated values, print the value of the middle node. For an even-length list, print the second middle node.
problems.inputFormat: One line of space-separated integers (non-empty list).
problems.outputFormat: Print the middle node's value.
hints: Slow/fast pointers: fast moves two steps, slow one; when fast ends, slow is at the middle.
For even lengths this lands on the second middle node.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists
problems.description: Given two sorted linked lists as space-separated values (one per line), merge them into one sorted list.
problems.inputFormat: Two lines: the first sorted list, then the second sorted list. Either line may be empty for an empty list.
problems.outputFormat: Print the merged sorted list, space-separated. Print an empty line if both lists are empty.
problems.constraints: 0 <= length of each list <= 10^5, values sorted non-decreasing

When one list runs out, append the rest of the other.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node from End of List
problems.description: Given a linked list as space-separated values and an integer n, remove the nth node from the end and print the remaining list.
problems.inputFormat: First line: space-separated integers (the list). Second line: integer n (1 <= n <= length).
problems.outputFormat: Print the remaining list, space-separated. Print an empty line if the list becomes empty.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    vals = list(map(int, lines[0].split())) if lines and lines[0].strip() else []
    n = int(lines[1]) if len(lines) > 1 else 1
    idx = len(vals) - n
    del vals[idx]
    print(' '.join(map(str, vals)))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: With real nodes, use two pointers n+1 apart: when the front pointer ends, the rear one is just before the target.
Removing the head is the special case handled by a dummy node.

problems.title: Reverse Nodes in K-Group
problems.description: Given a linked list as space-separated values and an integer k, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k, the remaining nodes stay in their original order.
problems.inputFormat: First line: space-separated integers (the list). Second line: integer k.
problems.outputFormat: Print the resulting list, space-separated. Print an empty line for an empty list.

referenceSolution.python:
def solve():
    import sys
    lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    vals = list(map(int, lines[0].split())) if lines and lines[0].strip() else []
    k = int(lines[1]) if len(lines) > 1 else 1
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(vals), k):
        chunk = vals[i:i + k]
        out.extend(reversed(chunk) if len(chunk) == k else chunk)
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

hints: Process the list in chunks of k, reversing each full chunk.
A final chunk smaller than k is left untouched.
